neon.tip: Cardinal and green neon have different red patterns from the true neon. Cardinal: the red stripe runs the whole length of the belly, from the gills to the tail. Neon: the red covers only the rear half of the body. Green neon: much smaller, with a short red patch near the tail.

rummy.tip: True rummy-nose (Hemigrammus): red on the nose only, with clean black-and-white tail bars. Brilliant/false rummy (Petitella): the red covers more of the head and the tail bars are bolder.

bigtetra.tip: Congo: big scales with a rainbow sheen, males have flowing fins. Emperor: dark stripe along the body, with a longer extended tail middle. Buenos Aires and black skirt tetras are deeper-bodied with dark bands.

skirt.tip: Black skirt: wide black fade at the rear and tall fins. Serpae: red-orange body with a black shoulder spot. Bleeding heart: a single red spot behind the gill on a pink body.

redbarb.tip: Rosy: copper-pink body with a black tail base spot in males that glow rosy red. Cherry: red body with a dark stripe through the eye. Tiger: four black vertical bars with orange-red fins. Odessa: red stripe along the middle of the body. Gold and checkerboard: golden or spotted.

algae.tip: Siamese algae eater: a clean black stripe from the nose through the eye all the way to the end of the tail. Flying fox: a gold stripe above the black one, and the stripe stops at the tail base. Chinese algae eater: golden, larger sucker mouth and a blotchy stripe, grows big and aggressive.

cory.tip: Skunk: black stripe along the back with an orange tint. Panda: black eye patches, black tail base and dorsal spot. Bronze/Aeneus: plain metallic bronze or green. Albino: pale pink with red eyes. Julii: spotted head with lines. False julii: more lines. Peppered: dark pepper spots over gray. Sterbai: dark with orange pectoral fins. Pygmy: under 1 inch, swims mid-water. Emerald (Brochis): longer-bodied and bigger than a bronze, with a bright metallic green-blue sheen and a taller dorsal fin.

loach.tip: Kuhli: thin eel-like with dark and tan bands. Clown: orange with black bands and red fins. Yoyo: marks that read "Y-O-Y-O" along the body. Zebra: pale with dark vertical stripes. Dojo/weather loach: long, plain, whiskered. Hillstream: flat, clings to glass.

rainbow.tip: Boesemani: front half blue-gray, back half orange-yellow. Turquoise: blue-green overall. Australian/splendid: stripe along the side with orange fins. Dwarf neon: under 2 inches with a red-stripe fade. Red: all red males. Threadfin: very tall twin dorsal fins.

guppy.tip: Endler: under an inch and a half, bright pattern, small tail. Guppy: larger, big fan-like tail in many colors. Platy: stockier with a rounded tail. Swordtail: males have a long sword on the tail. Molly: larger and taller with a big dorsal fin. Variatus platy: slimmer and more angular than a common platy, often mixed yellow, orange and blue. Least killifish: tiny, around an inch, plain gray-olive.

danio.tip: Zebra: horizontal blue-white stripes. Pearl: pearly sheen with a pink stripe. Leopard: spots instead of stripes. White cloud: tiny with a red tail base and a gold stripe. Celestial pearl danio: tiny with pale spots on dark blue.

rasbora.tip: Harlequin: copper body with a black triangle. Lambchop: thinner, longer black wedge. Espei: red-orange with a black wedge that starts at the middle. Chili: tiny and bright red. Scissortail: black-and-white striped tail.

gourami.tip: Dwarf: small, with blue and red vertical stripes over the body, often a metallic blue-orange look, and thread-like pelvic fins. Honey: smaller and plain, yellow-orange to tan with a dark stripe along the belly in breeding males, and no stripes on the body. Pearl: pearly spots with a dark line from nose to tail. Three-spot/blue/gold: larger, with a spot mid-body and one at the tail base. Kissing: pink, with big lips. Neon blue and powder blue are color forms of the dwarf gourami, not a separate fish. Honey gourami males are yellow-orange, females plain tan.

pleco.tip: Bristlenose: fleshy tentacles on the snout. Common: very large with a sail-like dorsal fin. Clown pleco: small with orange bands. Zebra pleco: small, bold black-and-white stripes. Otocinclus: tiny with a dark stripe, a flat sucker.

stick.tip: Twig catfish (Farlowella): very thin like a twig, with a long pointed snout. Whiptail (Rineloricaria): flatter body with a long thin whip-like tail.

cichmal.tip: Yellow lab: bright yellow with a black dorsal edge. Red zebra: orange to peach with a blotchy pattern. Cobalt zebra: blue with dark bars. Demasoni: small, blue with thick black bars. Kenyi: males yellow-orange, females blue bars. Peacocks: brilliant solid colors, long pointed body.

cichsa.tip: Angelfish: tall with long trailing fins. Oscar: large, with an orange-patterned dark body and a tail spot. Convict: black and white vertical stripes. Jack Dempsey: dark with bright blue-green flecks. Severum: round, with a faint orange or gold tint. Blue acara: gray-blue with a vertical dark bar behind the gill and blue speckles. Firemouth: red throat and belly. Keyhole: tiny with a keyhole-shaped spot.

dwarfcich.tip: German blue ram: blue-yellow with a black spot behind the head and red fins. Bolivian ram: duller, with a stripe over the eye. Kribensis (Pelvicachromis): elongated body, a purple-pink belly in females, a dark stripe along the side and eye-spots in the tail. Apistogramma: small with a rounded tail, males show a dark horizontal stripe and a frilled dorsal.

tanganyika.tip: Julidochromis: elongated with black stripes. Princess (brichardi): elegant, with extended fins and a light blue edge. Shell dwellers: tiny, rest in shells. Cyprichromis: slender, free-swimming and in schools.

puffer.tip: Pea puffer: tiny yellow-green with brown spots. Figure-8: rounder, with a figure-8 pattern on its back. Both are small, rounded and slow-moving.

betta.tip: Betta males have long flowing fins; females and plakats have short fins. Paradise fish: striped with red and blue and a forked tail.

goldfish.tip: Common/comet: long body with a single tail. Fantail and Ryukin: rounded body with a double tail. Oranda: has a head hood. Koi: barbels and a wide range of colors.

shrimpf.tip: Cherry: bright red (Neocaridina). Crystal red and bee shrimp: bands of white with red or black, with a clear-white body. Rili: a cherry shrimp variety, red with large clear patches. Tiger: thin stripes with orange eyes. Blue bolt: blue bands. Amano: gray-clear with dotted lateral spots. Ghost/glass: fully transparent. Bamboo/wood: large and brown, with fan arms. Blue velvet: solid blue.

nerite.tip: Zebra nerite: black stripes on gold. Tiger nerite: bold dark stripes. Horned nerite: has little horns. Olive nerite: plain, with a speckled olive shell. Mystery/apple snail: large, round, smooth shell in gold, blue or ivory.

cfish.tip: Ocellaris: orange with three white bands and thin black edging. Percula: thicker black edging between bands and a more rounded body. Percula and ocellaris are very hard to tell apart from a photo; percula has 10 dorsal spines and ocellaris has 11. Maroon: dark red with a single bright stripe. Clarkii: darker body with a yellow tail. Tomato: bright red-orange, with a single patch behind the eye.

tang.tip: Yellow: all bright yellow. Regal/blue/hippo: blue with a black palette shape and yellow tail. Purple: purple with a yellow tail. Kole: dark with a gold ring around the eye. Sailfin: tall with a large dorsal sail. Powder blue: sky blue with a white face and yellow dorsal.

damsel.tip: Blue-green chromis: bright blue-green, shoals in groups. Yellowtail damsel: royal blue with a yellow tail. Domino: black with white spots. Three-stripe: white with three black bars. Azure: blue and yellow.

gobyb.tip: Firefish: white nose and a red tail with a long dorsal spike. Yellow watchman: yellow body with a long dorsal fin. Lawnmower blenny: brown with a sloped face. Tailspot blenny: spotted with a stripe on the tail. Bicolor blenny: two-tone, with a dark head and yellow tail.

mandarin.tip: Mandarin: orange, blue and green swirls, slow along the rock. Psychedelic mandarin: the same but with a more intense maze-like pattern.

wrasse.tip: Six-line wrasse: six stripes. Melanurus: a black tail spot. Fairy wrasse: bright with long fins. Cleaner wrasse: thin blue stripe.

angel.tip: Flame angel: red-orange with vertical dark bars. Coral beauty: blue to orange with a dark shoulder. Bicolor: the front half is deep blue-purple and the back half is bright yellow, and it stays small. Rock beauty: yellow with a large black patch over the back and tail, and it grows much bigger. Lemonpeel: all yellow with a blue ring around the eye. Copperband butterfly: long snout with a copper-colored stripe.

euph.tip: Hammer: heads with hammer-shaped or anchor tentacle tips. Frogspawn: branching tentacle tips like frog eggs. Torch: long single-tipped tentacles. Duncan: short, round, fleshy polyps with a visible white stony skeleton below them, in a branching bush; not a plating coral.

softc.tip: Xenia: pulsing, waving stalks. Green star polyps: bright green mats with small arms. Kenya tree: a tree-like stalk branching into small heads. Leather (toadstool): wide, thick cap that folds in. Clove polyps: dense stalks with pale tips.

zoa.tip: Zoanthid/palythoa: groups of small round polyps in colonies and mats. Mushrooms (Discosoma): single smooth, flat discs with a slit mouth in the middle, no tentacles and no stalk. Ricordea: flatter bumpy disks. Rhodactis: larger and hairy-looking.

sps.tip: Acropora: branching with a tip polyp. Montipora: plating or encrusting with tiny polyps. Birdsnest/Seriatopora: thin fine branches. Stylophora: thick branches. Porites: smooth, stony fingers or plates with tiny round polyps. Cauliflower (Pocillopora): thick, bumpy branches with small wart-like bumps (verrucae) and no leafy plates. Pavona: leafy, layered plates. Montipora has no tip polyp, and its surface is covered in tiny rough pores.

lps.tip: Brain (Lobophyllia/Favia): round or dome-shaped with ridged, maze-like valleys. Trachyphyllia: flat and folded. Goniopora: long flowerpot-like polyps, delicate. Bubble coral: bubbly sacs. Candy cane: each polyp on its own stalk. Galaxea: clumps of long, hairy-looking sweeper tentacles on round polyps with a sharp stony wall. Cynarina/Scolymia: one big fleshy polyp with no tentacles.

anemone.tip: Bubble-tip: bulb tips on tentacles. Long tentacle: long flowing tentacles and a bigger body. Carpet: flat, wide, sticky tentacles. Condy: long, thin tentacles with pink tips. Aiptasia: tiny glassy pest.

crab.tip: Blue-leg hermit: blue legs with orange bands. Red-leg hermit: red legs. Emerald crab: green, mostly stationary. Sally Lightfoot: bright red and orange, runs fast.

reefsnail.tip: Turbo: large and round, with a rough shell. Nassarius: small cones that burrow. Astraea: flat coin-like shell. Cerith: thin spiral.

sword.tip: Amazon sword (Echinodorus): large, wide leaves growing from a crown. Narrow-leaf swords: thinner leaves. Often large and stand in the middle or back of the tank.

crypt.tip: Crypts form a rosette with crinkled leaves. Wendtii: wavy leaves in green to bronze. Parva: tiny and compact. Balansae: long, strap-like leaves.

val.tip: Vallisneria: long, thin ribbon leaves. Sagittaria: grass-like blades on a base, usually shorter. Jungle val: giant and broad. Madagascar lace plant (Aponogeton) is not a val: its leaves are a netted lattice with holes, like lace. Pygmy chain sword: short grass-like blades.

stem.tip: Ludwigia: oval leaves in pairs on a stem, red underside. Rotala: tiny narrow leaves in whorls, pink to red tips. Bacopa: thick round leaves. Hygrophila: pointy, often broad leaves. Alternanthera: red or maroon leaves. Hornwort looks feathery, with stiff whorls of thin forked needle-like leaves on a stem and no roots. Only call a plant Hornwort if the leaves are needle-like, not flat.

fern.tip: Java fern: finger-like fronds, small black spots under leaves. Anubias: thick dark arrowhead leaves. Mosses: green fuzzy mats on wood or rocks. Bolbitis: wavy dark fronds. Fissidens: tiny flat fern-like leaves in two neat rows, like little feathers. Flame moss: fine upright, flame-shaped growth with thin stringy stems.

float.tip: Frogbit: small round leaves with roots hanging down. Water lettuce: rosettes like tiny cabbages. Salvinia: round, hairy leaves. Duckweed: tiny dots covering the surface.

carpet.tip: Dwarf hairgrass: very fine grass-like carpet. Monte Carlo: rounded tiny leaves. Dwarf baby tears: tiny round leaves in a dense mat. Glosso: tiny paddle leaves.

macro.tip: Chaeto: fuzzy green balls or strands. Caulerpa: grape-like or feathery green runners. Halimeda: segmented, stiff.

geo.tip: Eartheaters have a sloped head, a downturned mouth and sift sand. Red-head types have a red-orange head; striped types have a dark band and spot. Many species look alike in stores, so the exact species is hard to tell from a photo.

cichca.tip: Texas: pearl-spotted, stocky and gray-blue. Jaguar: long with a big mouth and dark blotches. Midas and red devil: orange or gold with a nuchal hump. Salvini: yellow with a dark stripe. Rainbow cichlid: smaller with a gold body and dark stripes. Blood parrot: round orange hybrid with a beak-like mouth. Flowerhorn: a hybrid with a large forehead bump.

c.n: Easy, colorful LPS that likes to be fed. Low to medium light, low to medium flow.
One of the milder mbuna, silvery blue with a yellow tail. Likes rocks and can live with other peaceful Malawi cichlids.
Beautiful but difficult tang with an orange spot at the tail base. Needs a large tank, strong flow and very clean water.
Branching SPS that needs very stable, clean water and strong light and flow. For experienced keepers.
Elegant cory with an orange patch on the head. Needs a school, sand and clean water.
Mbuna with a blue body and a white or yellow top. Territorial. Keep in a crowded rocky tank.
Small, peaceful cichlid with a butterfly pattern. Good in a community tank with other peaceful fish.
Surface fish with wing-like fins that jumps and eats small fish. Needs a tight lid.
Colorful dwarf cichlid in many color forms. Keep one male with several females in a planted tank with caves.
c.f: Frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp, micro pellets

c.n: Electric blue males, a close cousin of the Electric Blue Hap. Peaceful with similar-sized fish.
c.f: Cichlid pellets, frozen mysis, brine shrimp

c.n: A pest anemone that spreads fast and stings corals. Peppermint shrimp and copperband butterflies eat it.
Pale pink version of the bronze cory. Hardy, social and best kept in groups.
Maroon-red stem plant that needs strong light and iron. Looks great in a planted tank.
Tall, delicate angelfish that needs warm, soft, acidic, very clean water. Not a beginner fish.
c.f: Cichlid pellets, frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp

c.n: Larger, excellent algae eaters. Tough and clean-minded, though larvae need brackish water to grow.
Floating plant with long, trailing roots. Shades the tank and soaks up nutrients; useful for shy fish.
Big, hardy background plant with broad leaves. Heavy root feeder, so use root tabs.
Fast, feathery stem plant that soaks up nutrients and shades out algae. Trim often. Easy for beginners.
Delicate stem plant with a red tint under bright light. Needs steady nutrients and CO2 to look its best.
Fast, easy stem plant that soaks up nutrients. Float it or plant it.
Tall, elegant cichlid that needs a tall tank. Adults may eat very small fish like neons; pairs defend breeding spots.
Colorful schooling fish that need feeding several times a day. Best for experienced keepers with larger tanks.
c.f: Frozen mysis and brine shrimp, fed several times a day

c.n: Tough, slow plant with dark leaves. Tie to wood or rock and do not bury the rhizome.
Small, colorful dwarf cichlid. Needs caves and plants; males hold territory.
c.f: Frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp, small pellets

c.n: Bulb plant with wavy leaves that likes a dormant spell. Good midground cover.
General plant entry. Look for the exact species name to see detailed care.
Shoots water at prey. Needs brackish water and a lid, and will eat small fish.
Eats bristle worms and fireworms. May pick off small fish and shrimp.
c.f: Bristle worms, frozen mysis, meaty foods

c.n: Hunts other snails. Use it to control pest snails, but not with snails you want to keep.
Algae-eating snail that grazes rock and glass. Hardy and good for nano tanks.
Very aggressive mbuna. Males turn black and gold, females yellow-gold. Best crowded with other mbuna in a large tank.
Active, silvery fish with orange fins. Needs a long tank, neutral to hard water and a group.
c.f: Flakes, small pellets, frozen brine shrimp

c.n: Bright blue and yellow damsel that gets territorial. Best with tough fish.
Hardy, thick stem plant with round leaves. Easy, good for beginners.
Looks small in stores but grows long and needs a large tank in a group of three or more.
Filter feeder that fans food from the current. Needs good flow and a mature tank.
c.f: Fine particles filtered from the water

c.n: Small lily with banana-shaped roots. Easy; do not bury the roots.
Hardy, active yellow wrasse that jumps. Needs a lid and may eat small ornamental shrimp.
Striking red and white shrimp that sometimes catches small fish. Territorial with others of its own kind.
c.f: Frozen mysis, brine shrimp, fish bits

c.n: Active rainbow with a dark horizontal band that colors up with age. Needs a school and hard, neutral to alkaline water.
c.f: Flakes, small pellets, frozen brine shrimp

c.n: Peaceful and calm, bred in captivity. Does best in pairs.
Flat, sand-colored catfish that buries itself. Needs soft sand and does not compete well for food.
c.f: Sinking pellets, frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp

c.n: Smaller, shy anthias that needs frequent feeding and a group of females.
c.f: Frozen mysis and copepods, fed often

c.n: Delicate black-and-white or red-and-white shrimp that need soft, stable, pure water. Not for beginners.
c.f: Biofilm, powdered shrimp food, algae wafers

c.n: Males flare at their own reflection and fight other males. Likes warm, calm water with plants and slow tank mates.
c.f: Betta pellets, frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp

c.n: Dwarf angel with a blue and yellow body. Can nibble corals, and aggressive toward similar angels.
Bold, two-toned blenny that lives in rock holes. May harass small, peaceful fish.
Long-snouted wrasse that picks at invertebrates and is fast. Needs a lid and a large tank.
Fine-branched SPS that is easier than acropora. Medium to strong light and flow.
Dwarf cichlid with a dark stripe and a blue-yellow body. Keep one male with several females.
c.f: Frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp, micro pellets

c.n: Large, heavy-bodied cichlid with a black belt. Can be aggressive. Needs a big tank.
Purple fish with a black cap that likes caves and ledges. Can be aggressive with similar shapes.
Black fancy goldfish with bulging eyes. Slow swimmer that needs gentle tank mates and lots of space.
Hardy little school fish from Paraguay with a bold black and silver stripe. Do best in groups of six or more with plants.
A dark morph of the percula. Hardy, easy and a great beginner reef fish.
Peaceful, hardy tetra from the Amazon. Keep six or more.
Active barb that can nip fins. Keep six or more so they pick on each other less than on other fish.
Hardy and active, with a habit of nipping slow, long-finned fish. Keep six or more with similarly quick tank mates.
Easy, colorful LPS that likes low light. Hardy and good for beginners.
Tall pink tetra with a red spot behind the gill. Peaceful in a group but can nip fins when kept in small numbers.
Pale, eyeless tetra that finds food and tank mates by feeling the water. Do not keep with fast, pushy fish.
Large tang with a yellow tail and orange spines. Needs a lot of swimming room.
A hybrid with a mouth that does not close well. Often dyed in stores. Can be pushy, so avoid small fish.
Hardy, silver tetra that may nip long fins. Likes cooler temperatures and a group.
Hardy cichlid with a blue-gray body and dark bar behind the gill. Needs a roomy tank and can bother small fish.
Striking bee shrimp with blue bands. Needs soft, acidic, mature water and no fish that eat shrimp.
c.f: Biofilm, powdered shrimp food, leaf litter

c.n: Large and bold, will eat fish it catches and uproot plants. Best alone or with fast fish.
c.f: Sinking pellets, blanched veggies, frozen meaty foods

c.n: Big, calm haplochromine with a lump on its head. Peaceful with fish its own size, and eats small ones.
Colorful killifish that jumps and may fight other males. Needs a lid and a calm tank.
Sensitive starfish that needs a mature tank and slow acclimation. Often dies in new tanks.
c.f: Biofilm and microfauna on live rock

c.n: Schooling, open-water cichlid from Lake Tanganyika. Keep six or more with peaceful tank mates.
Males shine bright blue; calmer than mbuna. Needs hard, alkaline water.
Peaceful blue-tinted tetra from the Amazon. Keep in groups of six or more.
Deep blue cousin of the cherry shrimp. Hardy, breeds easily in planted tanks without fish that eat shrimp.
Peaceful schooling fish that is easy to keep. Good in groups of five or more.
Algae cleaner that will take new snail shells. Needs spare shells.
Digs burrows, so needs deep sand and rubble. Peaceful and a jumper.
c.f: Frozen mysis, brine shrimp, meaty pellets

c.n: Blue in front and orange behind, calm and colorful. Likes neutral to hard water, a long tank and a group of six or more.
c.f: Flakes, small pellets, frozen brine shrimp

c.n: Dark, wavy fronds that grow on wood or stone. Slow starter but beautiful once settled.
Hardier than the German blue ram, peaceful and calm. Likes sand, plants and caves.
c.f: Cichlid pellets, frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp

c.n: Small, yellow dwarf cichlid. Hardy for an Apistogramma. One male per group of females.
c.f: Frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp, micro pellets

c.n: Open-water Malawi cichlid with a red-orange fin edge. Best in a long tank with a group of females per male.
c.f: Cichlid pellets, frozen mysis, brine shrimp

c.n: Easy, fleshy LPS that likes low to medium light. Can sting neighbors at night.
Small shell dweller that lives and breeds in snail shells. Needs sand and many empty shells.
c.f: Frozen brine shrimp, daphnia, micro pellets

c.n: The bolder-patterned cousin of the rummy-nose, schooling in open water. Keep warm, clean and in a group of eight or more.
Hitchhiking cleaner worm that eats waste. Usually helpful. Large fireworms are harmful, and bristles sting if handled.
Small, hardy pleco that eats algae and wood. Needs driftwood to chew and plenty of hiding spots.
Hardy scavenger that hides by day. Some species may grab small fish.
Hardy and common cory. Needs a group of six or more and smooth sand or gravel.
Bubble-like sacs by day and sweeper tentacles at night. Needs space and medium light, low flow.
Delicate goldfish with fluid-filled sacs under the eyes that burst easily. Needs a smooth, safe tank and gentle mates.
c.f: Soaked goldfish pellets, blanched greens, peas

c.n: Common host for clownfish. Needs strong light and a mature tank, and may wander and sting corals.
Slow, shimmery plant that grows on wood and rock. Hardy and good for nano tanks.
Hardy, active and plant-nibbling, best in a roomy tank. May bother small, slow tank mates.
c.f: Flakes plus blanched greens, frozen foods

c.n: Small, striped catfish that hides by day and eats tiny fish at night. Good with fish bigger than an inch.
c.f: Frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp, small fish

c.n: Black-and-yellow Malawi mbuna. Aggressive and territorial; needs hard water and rocks.
c.f: Small pellets, frozen brine shrimp, algae

c.n: Tiny brackish goby with bold stripes. Needs a little salt, caves and quiet tank mates.
Hardy, undemanding mouthbrooder. Males are bold, so keep one male with several females.
Feathery stem that needs good light and nutrients. Beautiful but often melts in poor conditions.
Dark Tanganyikan cichlid with white speckles that hunts in cracks. Needs rocks, sand and hard alkaline water.
Easy, hardy LPS that grows in clumps. Low to medium light, gentle flow.
Small, peaceful cichlid that needs soft, acidic, clean water. A good choice for a quiet planted tank.
c.f: Frozen daphnia, micro pellets, baby brine shrimp

c.n: Bright green, clover-like leaves on creeping stems. Prefers cooler water and melts in heat. Medium light.
Tall stem plant with bright red flowers if it grows above water. Likes medium light and cooler water.
Slightly larger and warmer-loving than the neon, from blackwater Amazon streams. Needs a school of eight or more, soft water and plants for cover.
Small striped wrasse that eats pests like Aspidistra and flatworms. Hardy and reef safe.
Huge and potent stinger that eats fish. Needs a large tank and experienced keeper.
Fast-growing macroalgae that can spread. Can go sexual and cloud the water, so keep it contained.
Fast-growing SPS shaped like cauliflower. Needs strong light, strong flow and stable alkalinity.
Tiny and shy, with a pearly spotted pattern. Prefers a calm planted tank and similarly gentle tank mates.
c.f: Crushed flakes, micro pellets, baby brine shrimp

c.n: Small, tough sand and rock cleaner. Good at eating diatoms and detritus.
c.f: Algae and film on sand and rock

c.n: Tangled, ball-like macroalgae that soaks up nutrients. Great in a refugium.
Colorful, spreading coral that likes low to medium light. Can sting neighbors.
Delicate, peaceful dwarf cichlid that needs soft, clean, acidic water and sand.
c.f: Frozen daphnia, micro pellets, baby brine shrimp

c.n: Peaceful, active barb with cool-water tolerance. Keep a group of six or more.
One of the gentlest barbs, red males show off in planted tanks. Keep six or more with calm tank mates.
Hardy, bright red shrimp that breed easily. Need moss, plants and no small-mouthed predators.
Small dwarf angel that may nip corals. Needs a mature tank.
Peaceful bristletooth tang that sifts algae and detritus from rock and sand.
Tiny and bright red; needs a calm nano tank and tiny, gentle tank mates. Keep a large group.
c.f: Crushed flakes, micro pellets, baby brine shrimp

c.n: Sold as an algae eater but gets large and aggressive. Often bullies other bottom fish.
Delicate, shy gourami that needs soft, acidic, very clean water. Not a beginner fish.
c.f: Frozen daphnia, micro pellets, baby brine shrimp

c.n: Slow moss with layered, drooping branches. Tie it to wood or rock. Shrimp love it.
Colorful filter feeder that burrows into live rock or coral. Needs good flow.
Brilliant red and green wrasse that eats small crustaceans and flatworms. Needs a lid and sand.
c.f: Frozen mysis, brine shrimp, small crustaceans

c.n: Red-brown clownfish that can be aggressive as it ages. Best kept as a bonded pair.
Tiny goby that perches on coral. Peaceful but can irritate some coral polyps.
Tough, adaptable clownfish that hosts many anemones. Can be bossy with other clownfish.
Cleans fish and eats scraps. Needs stable salinity and no copper.
c.f: Fish parasites, frozen mysis, meaty bits

c.n: Difficult; most starve in captivity. Not recommended for most aquariums.
c.f: Fish parasites; hard to feed in a tank

c.n: Hardy, easy polyps that wave their tentacles. Medium light and flow.
Ambush predator that swallows fish and shrimp whole, even ones nearly its own size. Keep it alone or with fish too big to eat.
c.f: Live or frozen fish and shrimp, fed every few days

c.n: Tiny, brightly marked top-water fish that eats tiny insects. Needs a lid and small, peaceful tank mates.
c.f: Frozen daphnia, mosquito larvae, baby brine shrimp

c.n: Sold small but grows huge and eats fish that fit in its mouth. Needs a very large tank.
Playful, social, long-lived loach that grows large. Needs a big tank, a group and plenty of hiding places.
Tiny, wood-eating pleco with orange bands. Needs real driftwood and caves.
Huge and aggressive. Eats corals and inverts, so only in fish-only tanks.
Striking blue mbuna from Lake Malawi. Needs hard, alkaline water and plenty of rockwork.
Popular dwarf cichlid with a ragged dorsal fin. Keep one male with several females in a planted tank with caves.
c.f: Frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp, micro pellets

c.n: Pretty urchin that covers itself in shells and bits of rock. Eats algae but may knock over frags and graze coralline algae.
Easy, fast soft coral with a branching tree shape. Handles lower light and spreads quickly.
A small shark-like catfish from brackish waters that grows large. Needs some salt as it matures.
Grows huge and makes lots of waste, despite its cute juvenile size. Needs a very large tank.
Tall, flat Tanganyikan predator that hides in crevices. Needs rock work and hard alkaline water.

Hardy butterflyfish with a black mask that eats corals and anemones. Best in fish-only tanks.
c.f: Frozen mysis, marine pellets, coral polyps

c.n: Hardy Central American cichlid that colors up when breeding. Can be pushy but is small and tough.
c.f: Cichlid pellets, frozen foods, some veggies

c.n: Native North American darter that needs cool, well-oxygenated water. Not for a heated tropical tank. Males squabble, so keep a small group.
Aggressive toward other bottom dwellers and its own kind. Best kept alone or with similarly large fish.
Hardy, breeds readily and cleans up leftovers. Some people find them a pest.
c.f: Algae, leftover food, dead plant matter

c.n: Real predator that will eat or bite tank mates. Illegal in some regions. Not for beginners.
Algae-eating mbuna with red cheeks. Aggressive and best kept with other mbuna.
Brackish crab that needs land to climb out onto. May catch fish and shrimp. Escapes easily.
Colorful Malawi cichlid, with red-orange males. Keep with other Malawi cichlids in hard, alkaline water.
Hardy silver tetra with a red upper eye. Active and peaceful, keep six or more.
Red macroalgae that soaks up nutrients and feeds tangs. Easy to grow.
Peaceful, colorful peacock cichlid with orange-red males. Keep one male with several females.
c.f: Cichlid pellets, frozen brine shrimp, mysis

c.n: Peaceful, with glowing red males in a group. Prefers harder water and plenty of swimming room.
c.f: Flakes, small pellets, frozen brine shrimp

c.n: Turns red under strong light. Likes nutrient-rich water and clear space at the surface.
Large, very aggressive cichlid with a red-orange belly. Needs a very large tank and strong tank mates.
Bold lily with red leaves. Pinches off pads that reach the surface.
Active mbuna from Lake Malawi. Needs hard alkaline water, rocks and a crowded-looking tank to spread aggression.
Hardy and common, but will take snail shells and may bother snails.
Territorial, aggressive and best kept alone. Needs hiding spots and a large tank.
Sold tiny but grows huge and eats plants and small fish. Needs a pond-sized tank.
c.f: Pellets, fruit, blanched veggies, fish pieces

c.n: Sand-sifting cichlid with a red head and a humped forehead in males. Needs a large tank with fine sand.
A giant predator sold as a tiny juvenile. Needs a pond-sized tank and eats most tank mates.
c.f: Large pellets, whole shrimp, fish pieces

c.n: Long, eel-like fish that breathes air at the surface. Hunts small fish at night, so keep the lid tight.
Beautiful but delicate angelfish that often refuses prepared foods. Experts only.
c.f: Sponges, frozen mysis; often refuses foods

c.n: Needs a large tank and a lot of swimming room. Prone to ich in new setups.
Hairy, large mushroom that tolerates a range of light. Hardy and fast growing.
Colorful, bumpy mushroom that likes low to medium light. Easy once settled.
Sensitive angelfish that eats sponges and often starves in captivity. Experts only.
c.f: Sponges, marine pellets; hard to feed

c.n: Small, colorful anemone that hides in rock. Needs medium light and rock to sit in. Can sting neighbors.
Hardy and active, males glow rosy red. Cooler water than most tropical fish; may nip slower fish with long fins.
Cool-water minnow that breeds with live freshwater mussels. Peaceful and does not need heat.
Cool-water feeder minnow. Hardy and peaceful, but does not suit warm tropical tanks.
Peaceful, silvery fish with a rosy flush on the fins. Best in a school of six or more.
Fine stem plant that turns pink to red under strong light. Better with CO2.
Purple and yellow dottyback. Bossy toward peaceful fish, so add it last.
c.f: Frozen mysis, brine shrimp, meaty pellets

c.n: Purple and yellow, hardy and peaceful with non-grammas. Needs caves and rocks to hide in.
Large wood-eating pleco. Needs driftwood, a big tank and clean water.
Calm algae eater with a sucker mouth. Needs wood and caves.
Hybrid peacock with a red-orange body. Males can be pushy. Best in a larger Malawi tank with a few females per male.
c.f: Cichlid pellets, frozen brine shrimp, mysis

c.n: Tight-schooling fish from the Amazon and a good water-quality canary. Likes soft, clean, warm water and a big group.
One of the calmer mbuna, rusty-orange to lavender. Needs rocks and hard water.
Clownfish with a pale saddle patch and a black body. Hardy, bonded pairs and more demanding than a common clown.
Often sold as a small plec but grows very large and makes a lot of waste. Needs a big tank.
Large and active, with a tall sail-like dorsal fin. Needs a big tank and lots of algae.
Fast, bold crab that eats algae and may snatch small fish or inverts.
Tiny, cool-tolerant cory that prefers a school of six or more on sand.
c.f: Crushed flakes, micro pellets, baby brine shrimp

c.n: Colorful and tough Central American cichlid. Aggressive with tank mates and likes caves.
Small, hairy floating plant. Easy and good for shading.
Needs a large mature sand bed and often starves in a new tank. Fine in a well-established reef.
c.f: Microfauna in sand; hard to feed

c.n: Small, hardy, cool-tolerant acara with blue spots. Pairs guard their patch. A good first dwarf cichlid.
c.f: Small pellets, frozen bloodworms, brine shrimp

c.n: Small mbuna. Males are blue with black bars, females yellow, and both are active and a little pushy.
Tiny, bright red male. Needs live or frozen food and a calm tank.
c.f: Frozen foods, live baby brine shrimp

c.n: Brackish schooling fish that eats plants. Needs salt and a big tank as it matures.
Larger, quick schooling fish with a black-and-white scissor tail. Needs a long tank and a lid.
Large single-polyp coral with vivid colors. Low light, gentle flow.
Hardy brown tang with a yellow tail base. Active and can be pushy with newcomers.
Can release toxins if stressed. Needs a mature tank with sand.
c.f: Detritus and film on the sand

c.n: Fast green macroalgae that grows in sheets. Good for a sump or refugium, but trim it so it does not take over.
Slow, delicate feeders needing calm, cool water and plenty of live food. Not with fast fish.
c.f: Frozen mysis, fed 2 to 3 times a day

c.n: Large anemone that needs a mature tank and strong light. It can wander and sting corals. For experienced keepers.
Ancient-looking predator that hunts at night. Needs a large tank, a tight lid and no small tank mates.
Hardy, striped damsel that gets bold with age. Aggressive toward more peaceful fish.
Lively red tetra that nips long fins if kept in small groups. Keep a school of eight or more and avoid long-finned tank mates.
Large, calm-for-a-cichlid fish with a round body. Needs a roomy tank and good filtration.
c.f: Cichlid pellets, blanched veggies, frozen foods

c.n: Tiny shrimp that sways its tail. Often lives on corals and anemones. Keep in groups.
c.f: Mysis, brine shrimp, fine meaty food

c.n: Calcified macroalgae shaped like a shaving brush. Needs sand to root in and steady calcium.
Tiny Tanganyikan cichlids that live in empty snail shells. Needs sand and shells, and hard, alkaline water.
c.f: Small pellets, frozen brine shrimp, mysis

c.n: Hardy, single-tailed calico goldfish. Active and messy. Does best in a large tank or pond.
Active, busy algae eater with a black stripe through the eye. Gets bigger than expected; keep in a small group.
c.f: Algae, algae wafers, some frozen foods

c.n: Giant surface predator that jumps and eats small fish. Needs a very large tank with a strong lid.
Big, peaceful and plant-eating schooler. Needs a large tank, open water and hardy plants.
Active, silvery fish with white-tipped fins that may nip long fins. Keep six or more.
Small shell and cave dweller with zebra stripes. Gets along in a Tanganyikan setup.
c.f: Frozen brine shrimp, daphnia, small pellets

c.n: Active and hardy, eats pests but can bully smaller fish. Needs a lid.
Peaceful, small clownfish with a white stripe down the back. Hardy and good for beginners, best as a pair.
Small, peaceful bottom feeder with a dark back stripe. Needs sand and a group of six or more.
Active loach with a skunk stripe. Keep in a group of five or more to limit squabbles.
Large, hardy gourami with a snakeskin pattern. Gets big and can be territorial with fish of similar shape.
White-spotted pleco that grows large. Likes driftwood and caves.
Eats shrimp and small fish. Needs a lid and large tank.
Pale blue, peaceful mbuna that is one of the gentler Malawi cichlids. Still needs hard, alkaline water.
Tiny gourami that makes clicks and grunts. Needs calm tank mates and floating plants.
Likes the top of the tank and jumps, so keep a tight lid. Peaceful in a group of six or more.
c.f: Floating flakes, small insects, frozen foods

c.n: Peaceful night-active cardinalfish with a spotted body. Keep a small group and feed after lights go off.
Blue-striped dottyback that is feisty and territorial. Best on its own.
Hardy, peaceful anthias with a square mark. Keep one male with several females and feed often.
c.f: Frozen mysis, brine shrimp, fed 3 times a day

c.n: Algae-eating blenny with a sloped face. Peaceful with other fish and good for clearing hair algae.
Compact, easy foreground or midground plant. Good for beginner scapes.
Warm-water cory with orange fins; a good match for discus tanks. Keep in groups.
Silvery predator that eats small fish. Needs a large tank and similar-sized tank mates.
Colorful dwarf cichlid with striped sides. Pairs defend a cave. Hardy and good in a small community.
Night-active, armored catfish with a talkative voice. May eat very small fish.
Peacock with yellow and blue males. Calmer than mbuna. Keep one male with several females.
c.f: Cichlid pellets, frozen brine shrimp, mysis

c.n: Thick-branched SPS that is a good first SPS. Needs strong light and good flow.
Frilly, dark green freshwater seaweed. Tie it to wood or rock. Hardy and slow growing.
No photosynthesis, so must be target fed every day. Very hard to keep long-term.
Bright yellow peacock and one of the mildest Malawi cichlids. One male per several females.
c.f: Cichlid pellets, frozen brine shrimp, mysis

c.n: Large eartheater with a striped body that sifts sand. Needs a big tank with fine sand.
c.f: Sinking pellets, frozen foods, sifted from sand

c.n: Shy red and white basslet that hides in caves. Peaceful and reef safe.
Active, hardy livebearers with a sword on the male's tail. Males can chase each other; keep more females than males.
Hardy, night-active African catfish. Species vary in size, so check which one you have.
Small, shy blenny that grazes on rocks. Hardy and good for reefs.
Fancy goldfish with bulging eyes and poor sight. Needs gentle tank mates and a tank free of sharp decor.
c.f: Soaked goldfish pellets, blanched greens, peas

c.n: Large, tough cichlid with pearl spots. Needs a large tank and aggressive tank mates.
Large, hardy cichlid with blue-green specks. Can eat small fish. Digs and sifts sand.
Butterflyfish with a pointed face that eats corals, anemones and worms. Can be fed in fish-only tanks.
Tall, double dorsal fins that spread like threads. Peaceful; keep in a calm tank.
c.f: Flakes, small pellets, frozen brine shrimp

c.n: Hardy and larger than most gouramis. Males can bully slower, smaller fish.
Hardy but aggressive as it grows. Best with other tough fish.
Bold fin-nippers. Only keep in a large group of eight or more and avoid long-finned fish such as bettas and angelfish.
Striped algae-eating snail. Needs hard water for a healthy shell and a lid.
c.f: Algae and film on glass and rock

c.n: A giant predator that is sold small. Needs a pond-sized tank and eats most tank mates.
Striped, orange-eyed shrimp that are tougher than bee shrimp. Stable water and gentle tank mates.
Large and very active. Needs a huge tank and tank mates of similar size.
c.f: Pellets, blanched greens, some live plants

c.n: Bright red and bold. Gets aggressive as it ages; best alone or as a bonded pair.
Small, hardy bristletooth tang that grazes algae. A good first tang for a medium tank.
c.f: Algae, film on rock, marine pellets

c.n: Long sweeping tentacles that sting neighbors. Medium light, gentle flow; needs space.
Folded, fleshy coral that sits on sand. Low to medium light, gentle flow.
Large, aggressive cichlid with three spots. Needs a large tank and tough tank mates.
Algae eater that rights itself if flipped. A good reef clean-up crew.
Tanganyikan algae-grazer that lives in big groups. Needs hard, alkaline, clean water and a rocky tank.
c.f: Spirulina flakes, algae-based foods; low protein

c.n: Powerful algae eater, though it can knock over frags. Needs rock to graze on.
Blue-green and active, easy to keep. Likes neutral to hard water, a long tank and a group of six or more.
c.f: Flakes, small pellets, frozen brine shrimp

c.n: Strong algae grazer that can knock over frags. Needs a stable, mature tank.
Slow, twig-like catfish that eats algae and biofilm. Needs a mature, well-oxygenated tank and calm tank mates.
c.f: Algae wafers, blanched veggies, frozen foods

c.n: Big, round, gentle cichlid with a black spot. Needs soft, warm, very clean water.
c.f: Cichlid pellets, blanched veggies, frozen foods

c.n: Odd catfish that swims belly-up and eats from the surface. Likes caves and groups.
Small puffer with saddles. May nip corals and clams and can be aggressive with other fish.
Tall, ribbon-like leaves that spread fast by runners. Good background plant for most tanks.
Big filter feeder, calm and shy. Needs good flow and a mature tank.
c.f: Fine particles filtered from the water

c.n: Hardy, cool-tolerant livebearer in many colors. Keep more females than males because males chase.
Large, predatory Malawi peacock-type. Needs a large tank and hard, alkaline water.
Large floating plant with thick roots. Needs strong light; pond plant sometimes sold for tanks.
Large, floating rosettes with long roots. Needs good light and a gap between the leaves and the lid.
Fast, feathery plant that can be floated or planted. Great for soaking up nutrients.
Easy stem plant with broad lace-like leaves. Fast grower that fills the background.
Slim, flat bottom dweller with a whip-like tail. Peaceful and slow, needs sand and wood.
c.f: Algae wafers, blanched veggies, frozen foods

c.n: Cool-water, hardy and peaceful schooling fish. Good for unheated tanks and beginners.
Peaceful wild-type betta that is less flashy than the common betta. Males do not usually fight as hard.
c.f: Frozen daphnia, mosquito larvae, micro pellets

c.n: Hardy, cold-tolerant moss. Tie it to wood or rock. Does well in cooler tanks.
Giant predatory cichlid that can reach over two feet. Only for very large tanks.
c.f: Large pellets, whole shrimp, fish pieces

c.n: Hardy, see-through tetra with a pale yellow glow. Does well in groups of six or more in a planted tank.
Pulsing coral that can grow fast and take over. Easy in some tanks, difficult in others.
Cube-shaped fish that releases toxin when stressed. Juveniles are bright yellow and sold small, but grow large.
Tiny yellow goby that perches on coral. May irritate coral and is sensitive to poor water.
Big wrasse that eats pests but also eats small inverts. Needs sand and a lid.
Bright yellow Malawi mbuna, active and territorial. Needs hard alkaline water and rock caves.
Bright golden neocaridina. Easy to keep in planted tanks with gentle tank mates.
Bright, active algae grazer that needs lots of swimming room. Does not mix well with other tangs of similar shape.
Sand-sifting goby that often pairs with a pistol shrimp. Needs sand and a lid.
Burrowing, mouth-brooding fish that needs deep sand or rubble and a lid. Reef safe.
Tough, boldly colored and territorial. Can harass peaceful tank mates.
Spotted wrasse that buries in sand at night. Needs a lid and a fine sand bed.
Active loach with a pattern that looks like Y-O-Y-O. Needs a group and cover; may eat snails.
Bold, striped fish that is nearly bulletproof. Very active, so give it open water and a tight lid.
Small striped loach, active and social. May eat snails; keep a group.
Barred mbuna in many color forms. Aggressive, best crowded with other mbuna. Needs rocks.
Excellent algae eater. Will not breed in fresh water; needs hard water for its shell.
c.f: Algae and film on glass and rock

c.n: Rare, tiny black-and-white pleco that needs warm, very clean water and caves.
c.f: Frozen bloodworms, sinking pellets, some veggies

c.n: Large spiny eel with a zigzag pattern. Eats small fish, needs soft sand and a tight lid.
Colorful, easy coral that grows in colonies. Contains palytoxin, so handle with gloves.
